mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth is positive, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when unemployment exceeds 5%, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate coupled with rising CPI indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when both conditions are met, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts during an expansion indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when housing starts increase, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when employment increases, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 indicates supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when industrial production is below 100, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales despite rising unemployment indicate conflicting economic signals, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when both conditions are met, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate during easing cycles stimulates economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when federal funds rate is low, more than 50% of the time.
